title: Full-profile observation vs. finite-N kriging: matrix theory does not cover continuum depth data ('N matches n' hand-waved)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Depth-handling subsection (option (ii) 'joint kriging in $(x,h)$' called 'exact') and Theorem `\label{thm:anticipated}` ('each borehole a full noiseless profile so $N$ matches $n$ via the depth treatment').

All kriging results in parts (b),(d) are proved for a **finite** data vector $\mathbf Y\in\mathbb R^N$ with an **invertible matrix** $\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ (the BLP/BLUP proofs explicitly use $\Sigma\succ0$ and $\Sigma^{-1}$). A *full noiseless depth profile* at a borehole is a **continuum** of observations on the interval $I$, i.e. functional data; the matching predictor is an infinite-dimensional ($L^2(\Omega)$ / Hilbert-space) kriging problem with a covariance **operator**, not an $N\times N$ inverse. The phrase 'N matches n' does not reconcile a finite matrix theory with continuum data, so option (ii) is not justified by the proved theorems, and Theorem thm:anticipated's sample-size bookkeeping is unsupported.

**Suggested fix.** Either (a) commit to finitely many sampled depths per borehole, so $N=\sum_i p_i<\infty$ and the matrix theory applies — but then keep the within-hole quadrature/integration error of option (i) explicitly in every MSE budget (it is not zero); or (b) develop continuous BLP: data span a closed subspace $H_{\mathbf Y}\subset L^2(\Omega)$, $\widehat R=\Pi_{H_{\mathbf Y}}R$, kriging variance $=\|R-\Pi_{H_{\mathbf Y}}R\|^2$, with existence justified via a Karhunen–Loève expansion of the field.
